_README: Field markup captured read-only from real application forms George was about to fill, 2026-08-04. Nothing was typed and nothing was submitted. Each field records only what the autofill engine can actually see: label text, aria-label, placeholder, name, id, type. Use these as regression fixtures so the matcher is tested against forms that exist rather than forms we imagined.

greenhouse_array_it_specialist.notes: Screener questions render as a visible input[type=text] with id=question_<id>, each followed by an unnamed input[required] with no label — Greenhouse's combobox pattern. The unnamed sibling is what validation checks.

breezy_transact_campus_support_engineer.notes: AngularJS form. Repeating Experience and Education rows carry NO name, NO id and NO index — the only identifier is the placeholder. The two date inputs in each row inherit placeholder='Company', so placeholder matching alone puts a company name into a date field.

workable_bes_software_it_specialist.notes: BEHAVIOURAL FINDING, not a field capture. The page has an 'Apply now' button and a 'Submit application' button in the DOM, but zero input/select/textarea elements — including hidden ones — until the modal genuinely mounts. No shadow DOM, no iframe. Autofill run before the modal opens finds nothing and reports 0 of 0 fields, which looks like a failure but is a timing problem.

jobvite_ima_group_web_developer.notes: Reconstructed from a live mobile screenshot (2026-08), not a DOM capture. Jobvite renders placeholder-labelled inputs with a trailing required asterisk and no <label> elements; resume upload is a styled SELECT dropdown over a hidden file input; reCAPTCHA present.
